name: Dravsin Mango-Szechuan Pebbles
description: Tiny, pebble-shaped hard candies with a mango candy shell that shatters into a Szechuan peppercorn-laced center, producing the characteristic numbing tingle alongside a mild natural-extract stimulant. Sold in 25g tins.
flavor_profile: Sweet mango shell cracking open to a tingling, numbing Szechuan heat with a bright citrus undertone — the tingle lasts two to three minutes
cultural_context: Dravsin Pebbles have a devoted following among BCI-augmented users who report that the Szechuan tingle creates a subjectively interesting interference pattern with low-level sensory augmentation. This is almost certainly psychosomatic, but the community around it is real — there are dedicated forums and flavor-chasing subcultures built around pairing Pebbles with specific BCI modes.
story_hooks: A BCI researcher has discovered that the Szechuan compound in Dravsin Pebbles does have a measurable, minor effect on certain augmentation chipsets — not dangerous, but enough that a corponation wants the data suppressed before it complicates their augment certification process.
The online community around Dravsin Pebbles and BCI pairing has been infiltrated by someone using the forum to identify high-value augmented targets for a chrome-theft operation.

Dravsin Snack Works is a tiny independent manufacturer with exactly one product — a corponation acquisition offer has just arrived, and the owner, a retired Tier 1 street vendor, has no idea how to evaluate it or who to trust.
